tool.name: hgt-site
tool.description: call candidate horizontal gene transfer sites from host alignments, with a classifier or a known sequence
tool.command: #if $alignment.is_of_type('sam') ln -s '$alignment' input.sam && #set $aln = 'input.sam' #else ln -s '$alignment' input.bam && ## Only a coordinate sorted BAM carries an index, and hgt-site needs one ## to find exact junctions from split reads. Without it junctions are ## placed from read pairs alone, which still works. #if $alignment.is_of_type('bam') ln -s '$alignment.metadata.bam_index' input.bam.bai && #end if #set $aln = 'input.bam' #end if hgt-site call --bam '$aln' #if $foreign.source == 'classifier' --classifications #for $k in $foreign.classifications '$k' #end for #else --donor '$foreign.donor' #if str($foreign.donor_taxid) --donor-taxid $foreign.donor_taxid #end if #if $foreign.source == 'long_reads' --long-reads #end if #end if #if $control.use == 'yes' --control '$control.table' --control-min-pairs $control.control_min_pairs --control-window $control.control_window #end if --host-taxid $host_taxid #if $taxonomy.source == 'cached' --nodes '$taxonomy.nodes.fields.path/nodes.dmp' #elif $taxonomy.source == 'history' --nodes '$taxonomy.nodes' #end if --threads "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" --min-mapq $advanced.min_mapq --min-support $advanced.min_support --max-qvalue $advanced.max_qvalue -o '$sites' --bed '$bed' --vcf '$vcf'

param.name: alignment
param.label: Reads aligned to the host genome
param.help: Paired-end short reads, or long reads if you pick that below. Any sort order works. A coordinate sorted BAM carries an index, which lets the tool find exact junctions from split reads; without one, junctions are placed from read pairs alone.

param.name: source
param.label: How the foreign reads are identified
param.option: A taxonomic classifier ran on the unmapped reads
A sequence I already have, such as a vector or viral genome
A sequence I already have, and the reads are long reads

param.name: classifications
param.label: Per-read taxonomic calls for the unmapped reads
param.help: Per-read output from Kraken2, KrakenUniq, Kaiju, Centrifuge, DIAMOND or BLAST, or a two-column file of read name and taxid. Not a Kraken2 report. The format is detected from the file. Read names must match the alignment. Several files can be selected if a pipeline wrote more than one per sample.

param.label: NCBI taxonomy ID of the host
param.help: For example 9606 for human or 10090 for mouse.

param.name: use
param.label: Compare against a matched control
param.help: For a tumour and the normal tissue from the same person. Call the normal first, then give its table here: a position producing foreign reads in both samples is not somatic.
param.option: Yes, flag anything the control also has

param.name: table
param.label: hgt-site table from the matched control
param.help: The candidate sites table hgt-site produced for the control sample.

param.label: Supporting reads a control candidate needs before it counts
param.help: A control sample carries thousands of weak candidates from chance chimeras, roughly one per kilobase, so lowering this much below five rejects real sites along with the artefacts.

param.label: How far a control candidate may sit from a site and still count as the same position

param.name: source
param.label: NCBI taxonomy
param.help: With the NCBI taxonomy, reads classified anywhere in the host lineage are ignored, not only those assigned to the host taxid itself.
param.option: Use a nodes.dmp from the history

Minimum supporting read pairs for a site
Maximum q-value of the enrichment test

tool.help:
**What it does**
hgt-site finds places where DNA from bacteria or other organisms may have been inserted into a host genome, using paired-end sequencing data. Most bacterial reads in these samples come from contamination or from DNA fragments joined by chance in the lab, so hgt-site checks each possible site against what chance alone would produce and keeps only the sites with clearly more support.
**Inputs**
- Reads aligned to the host genome (BAM or SAM). - The NCBI taxonomy ID of the host. - One of two ways to say which reads are foreign: - per-read taxonomic calls for the reads that did not map to the host, from Kraken2, KrakenUniq, Kaiju, Centrifuge, DIAMOND or BLAST, or a two-column file of read name and taxid. The format is worked out from the file, and read names must match those in the alignment; or - a FASTA of the sequence you are looking for, such as a vector, a transgene or a viral genome. The unmapped reads are matched against it directly, so no classifier and no classifier database are needed.
**Long reads**
Nanopore and PacBio reads work too, as the third option under "How the foreign reads are identified". A long read crossing an integration is clipped at the junction by the aligner, and the clip boundary gives the position directly rather than from a pair, which is why this needs the sequence rather than a classifier. On simulated nanopore reads at 15x coverage it found 20 of 20 insertions with nothing false, the junction a median of 4 bp from the truth.
**A matched control**
For a tumour and the normal tissue from the same person, call the normal first and give its table under "Compare against a matched control". A position producing foreign reads in both samples is not somatic, and is reported as ``IN_CONTROL`` rather than passing. On a simulated pair sharing a region at six copies this removed all eight false sites for the cost of one real one. The control needs five supporting reads within 300 bases before it counts; lowering that much is a mistake, because a control sample carries thousands of weak candidates from chance chimeras.
**Outputs**
- A table with one row per candidate site: position, supporting read pairs, main foreign taxon, enrichment statistics, flags, and a filter column that says PASS or lists the reasons a site failed. - A BED file of the sites that passed every filter. - A VCF file of every candidate site, with PASS or the failing flags in the FILTER column.
**Reading the results**
Four columns decide whether a site is worth following up: ``n_pairs`` against ``expected_pairs``, which is how many pairs chance alone would have put there; ``qvalue``; ``top_taxid_fraction``, where a value near 1.0 means the support comes from one organism; and the split-read counts, where any at all is the strongest evidence in the table.
A site that passed is a lead rather than a finding. hgt-site has been validated on simulated reads from real genomes and not on real sequencing data with confirmed integrations.
**More**
Documentation: https://iraajgangavaram.github.io/hgt-site/
Benchmarks and source: https://github.com/iraajgangavaram/hgt-site
